title: The failure of COP31 leaves an urgent question: will it ever be possible to agree on the end of fossil fuels?
description: “The lack of an agreement should not be considered a failure, but rather a successful defense of the integrity of the UN climate agency in the face of a coordinated attack by a few countries radically opposed to action against climate change,” said the director of Climate Analytics, Bill Hare, who argued: “Countries committed to a safer future drew a red line and refused to sign a document that did not include any reference to the phase-out of fossil fuels, but that, instead, proposed a large-scale carbon capture and storage goal. This was clearly unacceptable, and the countries that refused to accept it were right to do so.”
